label: Keycloak
note: Keycloak (self-hosted or managed). Guidance covers authenticators, brute-force defences, token and session handling, client credentials, and deployment hardening.

questions.label: Authenticators / MFA
questions.text: Which authentication methods are required in the browser flow? (select all that apply)

guidance.text: **Strong posture.** WebAuthn passwordless / passkeys are phishing-resistant. Enable them under Authentication > Policies > WebAuthn Passwordless Policy and require them in the browser flow for sensitive clients.
**Good.** TOTP is a solid factor. Set OTP as a required action (or conditional OTP in the browser flow) and consider adding WebAuthn/passkeys for phishing resistance.
**GAP.** Password-only. Add a second factor: configure the browser flow with conditional OTP or enable WebAuthn/passkeys, and set a strong password policy.
**GAP.** No MFA. Configure the browser authentication flow to require OTP or WebAuthn; requiring OTP is the recommended mitigation against password guessing.

questions.label: Brute-force detection
questions.text: Is realm brute-force detection enabled (Realm settings > Security defenses), together with a password policy?

options.label: Enabled (lockout / backoff) plus a password policy

guidance.text: **GAP.** Brute-force detection is off by default. Enable it under Realm settings > Security defenses > Brute Force Detection (temporary lockout with backoff), set a complex password policy, and add reverse-proxy rate limiting for volumetric attacks.

**Review.** Finish the configuration: prefer temporary lockout with progressive backoff (permanent lockout invites denial-of-service), set a password policy, and forward LOGIN_ERROR and lockout events to your SIEM.
**Good.** Brute-force detection and a password policy are in place. Keep lockout temporary rather than permanent, and pair with reverse-proxy rate limiting and event monitoring.

questions.label: Tokens & sessions
questions.text: How are token lifespans and refresh tokens configured?

options.label: Short access tokens, refresh-token rotation (Revoke Refresh Token), bounded SSO session

guidance.text: **Review.** Shorten the access-token lifespan, enable 'Revoke Refresh Token' (rotation) so reused tokens are detected, keep the authorization-code lifespan short (under ~10s), and bound SSO session idle/max. Consider DPoP for sender-constrained tokens.
**Review.** Confirm token lifespans (Realm settings > Tokens), enable refresh-token rotation, and set SSO session idle/max proportionate to risk.
**Good.** Short-lived tokens with refresh rotation and bounded sessions support reuse detection. Validate token signature, issuer, and audience in resource servers.

questions.label: Client credentials
questions.text: How are OAuth clients configured for browser / native (public) apps?

options.label: Public client with PKCE (proof key required)
Confidential client, secret server-side (or mTLS / private_key_jwt)
A secret, or no PKCE, on a public client

guidance.text: **GAP.** Public clients must use PKCE and hold no usable secret. Enable Proof Key for Code Exchange and register specific (non-wildcard) redirect URIs to prevent open-redirect and code-interception attacks.
**Good.** Public clients use PKCE; confidential clients keep secrets server-side (or use mTLS / private_key_jwt). Keep redirect URIs specific.

questions.label: Deployment hardening
questions.text: For a self-hosted deployment: is TLS enforced and the admin console / REST API restricted?

options.label: HTTPS enforced, admin endpoints not public, default admin changed, production mode

guidance.text: **GAP.** Do not run a dev/default posture in production. Enforce HTTPS everywhere, run Keycloak in production mode behind a reverse proxy, keep the admin console / REST API off the public internet, and change the default admin credentials.
**Review.** Close the gaps: require SSL for all realms, restrict the admin console / REST API to trusted networks, set browser security headers (HSTS, CSP) at the proxy, and pin the Keycloak version.
**Good.** TLS enforced, admin surface restricted, production mode. Keep the version patched (track Keycloak CVEs) and monitor admin events.
